data.title: Final reminder before enforcement – broadcasting fee arrears (likely scam)
data.summary: A letter claiming to be from a "Rundfunk Zahlungszentrale" demands €254.35 in broadcasting fee arrears within 48 hours of receipt, to a Lithuanian IBAN. It has several strong scam indicators.
data.explanation: The letter says you owe €254.35 in broadcasting fees (Rundfunkbeitrag), late fees and processing fees. It demands payment within 48 hours and threatens account and wage garnishment. It looks like a scam. The payment account is Lithuanian (LT), which is unusual for a German broadcasting body. The 48-hour deadline is pressure, and you are told not to contact the normal Beitragsservice. Don't pay yet. Check your fee account directly with the real Beitragsservice Musterstadt, using contact details you already know or the official website. Don't use the e-mail address in this letter. If you get a real notice, note that you may have legal remedies. Consider reporting this letter to the police or a consumer advice centre.

warnings: The payee IBAN is Lithuanian (LT), not German, which is very unusual for a German broadcasting body.
The payee is named 'Beitragsinkasso UAB', a foreign company form, not a public broadcaster.
A 48-hour payment deadline and threats of garnishment without further notice are typical pressure tactics.
The letter tells you not to contact the known Beitragsservice address and to use only an e-mail, which is a scam pattern.
The salutation 'Sehr geehrte Herr Rivera' is grammatically wrong and the sender name looks unofficial; a real fee notice normally comes from Beitragsservice with a fee-notice and remedy instructions.
Verify the claim with the real Beitragsservice before paying anything.
